summary: The main design gap is that local MCP currently bypasses the ToolManager credential and permission pipeline entirely. The highest risks are token handling, unresolved identity contracts, agentd privilege boundaries, and insufficiently defined device/connect completion protocols.

suggestions.title: Make the ToolManager boundary real for stdio
suggestions.rationale: `MCPServerBase.handle_tools_call` invokes `MCPToolAdapter.execute`, which calls `tool._execute` directly. This bypasses `AbstractTool.execute`, `ToolManager.set_broker`, permission checks, credential injection, and lifecycle hooks. Bind one process-scoped PermissionContext and broker through a ToolManager-backed adapter, then test a credentialed tool end-to-end.

suggestions.title: Define structured MCP auth-required output
suggestions.rationale: The current adapter catches exceptions and renders text; ToolResult metadata is emitted as a second text item. That does not guarantee that `AuthRequiredPayload` fields such as `user_code`, `verification_uri`, and `expires_in` remain machine-readable to Claude Code or Codex. Specify one MCP result envelope and test every field survives serialization without stdout contamination.

suggestions.title: Resolve the agentd channel contract
suggestions.rationale: The S-1 contract lists `cli` but not `agentd`, while the existing UDS resolver creates `PermissionContext(channel="agentd")`. Reusing `CliPrincipalResolver` is ambiguous: either add `agentd` as a supported origin or use `channel="cli"` with a separate transport/origin field, and define the audit semantics explicitly.

suggestions.title: Do not make login-token-derived encryption the only cache boundary
suggestions.rationale: A local cache encrypted solely from the login token means possession of both the login file and cache decrypts provider credentials, while token rotation can make the cache unrecoverable. The existing Jira file store is only mode-0600 plaintext JSON, whereas the MCP Vault store delegates encryption to the server vault. Prefer OS keyring/DPAPI/Keychain-backed envelope keys, with explicit rotation and recovery behavior.

suggestions.title: Pull access tokens only; keep refresh tokens server-side
suggestions.rationale: The proposed token-pull policy is still open, but both existing local Jira storage and the O365 resolver handle refresh tokens as durable secrets. Returning refresh tokens to every stdio process materially expands the blast radius. Make the endpoint return short-lived access tokens plus expiry, require PBAC and audit on each pull, and refresh only through the server.

suggestions.title: Freeze the login-token and identity-endpoint contract first
suggestions.rationale: `principal_guard` accepts several authentication modes, while the transport maps navigator-auth sessions and external introspection tokens differently; `resolve_user_id` is backend-dependent. A generic resolver cannot safely assume that a session token, API key, or external bearer yields the same Navigator principal. Specify token audience, scope, expiry, revocation, tenant response, and failure status before implementing `parrot login`.

suggestions.title: Return roles or scopes with CLI principal resolution
suggestions.rationale: The current CLI context uses an empty role set, while server principal resolution derives roles from token scopes and `build_principal_context` otherwise defaults to empty roles. If local ToolManager enforcement is enabled, omitting server-issued roles causes legitimate calls to deny or encourages a later fail-open workaround. The identity endpoint should return authoritative roles/scopes and the resolver should pass them explicitly.

suggestions.title: Specify RFC 8628 as a typed engine, not only a URL field
suggestions.rationale: The existing O365 implementation delegates polling and provider-specific behavior to `interactive_login`, with a callback that prints to stdout. A generic engine needs a challenge model, polling interval, `authorization_pending`/`slow_down`/expiry handling, cancellation, timeout, and token persistence boundaries. Define that protocol before adapting O365 and adding Google support.

suggestions.title: Keep local cache I/O off the event loop
suggestions.rationale: `LocalJiraTokenStore` performs synchronous file reads, writes, directory creation, and `flock` operations, and its resolver calls them from async methods. A generalized cache used by concurrent stdio calls must use `asyncio.to_thread` or an async storage implementation, plus single-flight refresh and cancellation-safe lock release.

suggestions.title: Correlate connect polling with an attempt
suggestions.rationale: Polling `GET /api/v1/connections` by provider can observe an older active connection or the wrong account and cannot distinguish completion from a pre-existing state. Have `start` return an attempt/state identifier and poll a provider-plus-attempt status, while retaining the Jira-style state validation for paste completion.

suggestions.title: Do not make agentd read arbitrary peer home directories implicitly
suggestions.rationale: The current agentd process obtains the peer username and falls back to a configured service identity. Having a daemon read that user's `~/.parrot` file requires filesystem access the daemon may not have, or root-like privileges that create a confused-deputy risk. Specify ownership, permission, symlink, missing-file, and fallback behavior; consider a client-authenticated envelope or per-user daemon instead.

suggestions.title: Keep server-proxy REPL identity bearer-owned
suggestions.rationale: `ServerAgentProxy` deliberately omits `user_id`, has a no-op `configure`, and authenticates every request from its bearer header. A local `CliPrincipalResolver` should apply to standalone agents and local MCP, not override or duplicate identity in `--server` mode; otherwise local and remote principals can diverge silently.
